title: Nise da Silveira's birth chart
metaDescription: Nise da Silveira's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 26.3° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Jupiter sit 0.1° from an exact sextile — near enough that the tradition reads identity and expansion as a single working part. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aquarius, but precisely: 26.3°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Venus in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aquarius (9.6°), Venus in Aries (12.9°), Mars in Scorpio (14.8°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Jupiter is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.1°. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Saturn at 2.4°, and the Sun conjunction Saturn at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 26.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Aries at 12.9° is in detriment; Mars in Scorpio at 14.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Aquarius at 23.8° is in domicile. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in air, 2 in fire, 2 in water, 1 in earth by element, 4 fixed, 4 cardinal, 1 mutable by modality. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Gemini into Cancer during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.4° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
